step1_analysis.circuit_type: Neuromorphic pixel front-end / Integrate-and-fire spike generator
step1_analysis.description: A silicon retina pixel circuit that extracts spatial gradients using a spike-based charge pump. It features an asynchronous spike generator (oscillator) and a frequency-to-voltage converter (charge pump) driven by the photoreceptor input.

paper_reference.title: A 100 100 Pixel Silicon Retina for Gradient Extraction With Steering Filter Capabilities and Temporal Output Coding

delay_N5_N0.description: Delay from bias N5 to output N0, characterizing the spike generator's response time.

sky130_expected.calculation: Simulated delay in 130nm node with 1.8V supply.
sky130_expected.reasoning: SKY130 is significantly faster than the original 0.5um process, so the 60ns delay reported in the paper will likely scale down to a few nanoseconds.

delay_LABEL_N1.description: Delay from input LABEL_NET_0 to integration node N1.

sky130_expected.calculation: RC delay of the integration node.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends on the parasitic capacitance at N1 and the pull-up current from XM11. Note that XM14 acts as a diode clamp, limiting N1 to ~|Vthp| (0.4V - 0.6V).

power_avg.description: Average power consumption of the pixel.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Power scales down with technology, but depends heavily on the bias voltages applied and the spike rate.

v_n1_max.description: Maximum voltage reached at the integration node N1.

sky130_expected.calculation: Clamped by XM14 (PMOS diode to GND).
sky130_expected.reasoning: XM14 has its gate and drain tied to GND and source to N1. It will conduct when N1 exceeds |Vthp|, clamping the node voltage.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to measure the response delays of the spike generator and charge pump, as well as average power consumption.
